name: Faroese

ancestors.notes: Danish adstrate — administrative language until 1948; heavy lexical influence

notes:
Faroese (føroyskt), ~50,000 speakers in the Faroe Islands, Old West Norse descent alongside Icelandic. Hammershaimb's etymological orthography puts a large distance between spelling and sound, so the spec leans on positional entries rather than a flat grapheme table.

QUANTITY. Every stressed vowel letter has two realisations that differ in QUALITY, not only in length: the long one in an open stressed syllable, the short one before a geminate or a consonant cluster. ⟨a⟩ is [ɛaː]/[a], ⟨á⟩ [ɔaː]/[ɔ], ⟨e⟩ [eː]/[ɛ], ⟨i y⟩ [iː]/[ɪ], ⟨í ý⟩ [ʊiː]/[ʊj], ⟨o⟩ [oː]/[ɔ], ⟨ó⟩ [ɔuː]/[œ], ⟨u⟩ [uː]/[ʊ], ⟨ú⟩ [ʉuː]/[ʏ], ⟨ø⟩ [øː]/[œ]. The long values sit in nucleus_stressed and the shortening before a cluster is an allophone rule (Thrainsson, Petersen, Jacobsen & Hansen 2004; Arnason 2011).

STOPS. Faroese has no voice contrast in stops; the contrast is aspiration. ⟨b d g⟩ are the unaspirated [p t k] and ⟨p t k⟩ are aspirated only in the word-initial onset — a medial or post-⟨s⟩ stop is plain. ⟨pp tt kk⟩ are preaspirated [ʰpp ʰtt ʰkk] (Arnason 2011).

PALATALISATION. ⟨k g sk⟩ become [tʃʰ tʃ ʃ] before ⟨e i y⟩ and in the digraphs ⟨kj gj ggj skj sj⟩, but not before ⟨í ý⟩ — that pair patterns as a back-onset diphthong [ʊi], not a front vowel, and the velar survives (⟨kíkur⟩ [kʰʊiːkʊɹ], ⟨skína⟩ [skʊiːna]). The inherited diphthong spellings ⟨kei koy gei goy skei skoy⟩ likewise block it and keep the velar; ⟨ey⟩ does not block it (⟨geykur⟩ [tʃɛiːkʊɹ], ⟨skeyt⟩ [ʃɛiːt]). ⟨hj⟩ is [j] (Thrainsson, Petersen, Jacobsen & Hansen 2004).

SKERPING. The Verschärfung spellings ⟨ógv úgv⟩ are [ɛkv] and [ɪkv] — the vowel changes quality and a stop appears, which no compositional reading of the letters gives, so they are grapheme units (Arnason 2011).

RHOTIC AND ⟨ð⟩. /r/ is the alveolar approximant [ɹ], not a trill. ⟨ð⟩ is silent by default and surfaces as the glide [j] between vowels, with [v] and [w] as further allophones (Lockwood 1955; Thrainsson, Petersen, Jacobsen & Hansen 2004). WikiPron gold favours [w] after a rounded vowel and [v]/[j] elsewhere, but that conditioning is not stated in the cited sources and the spec does not encode it; [j] is the 1-best.

NOT ENCODED. Retroflex assimilation of ⟨rn rs rt rl rd⟩ and the stop insertion that turns ⟨rn⟩ into [tn] are both real and both variable, and the WikiPron gold splits between them word by word; encoding either one as categorical would state something the sources do not. Danish loanwords keep unpalatalised velars and plain [a] where a native word would palatalise or diphthongise, and the spec has no loan lexicon to separate them. Secondary stress in compounds is not encoded: ⟨nucleus_stressed⟩ fires only on the word-initial syllable, so a second or later stem in a compound never gets its long vowel, which is the largest single error class against WikiPron gold (352 of 354 gold rows with two or more length marks come out short).

stress.notes: Faroese has categorical word-initial stress; the acute-accented letters mark vowel quality, not stress placement (Thrainsson, Petersen, Jacobsen & Hansen 2004).
